claim: CD8+ tissue-resident memory T (CD8+ Trm) cells play key roles in many immune-inflammation-related diseases.
source: CD8 + tissue-resident memory T (CD8 + Trm) cells play key roles in many immune-inflammation-related diseases.
evidence: This is a general statement supported by established scientific knowledge in the field of immunology.

claim: CD8+ Trm cells were predominantly located in the lamina propria adjacent to the basement membrane in oral lichen planus.
source: we revealed that CD8 + Trm cells were predominantly located in the lamina propria adjacent to the basement membrane
evidence: This claim is supported by single-cell RNA sequencing profiling and spatial transcriptomics data presented in the study.

claim: CD8+ Trm cells were significantly increased in patients with erosive oral lichen planus (EOLP) compared to those with non-erosive oral lichen planus (NEOLP).
source: CD8 + Trm cells were predominantly located in the lamina propria adjacent to the basement membrane and were significantly increased in patients with erosive oral lichen planus (EOLP) compared to those with non-erosive oral lichen planus (NEOLP).
evidence: This is supported by single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics data, as well as flow cytometry results shown in Figure 5.

claim: CD8+ Trm cells displayed enhanced cytokine production, including IFN-γ, TNF-α, and IL-17, in patients with EOLP.
source: Furthermore, these cells displayed enhanced cytokine production, including IFN-γ (Interferon-gamma, a pro-inflammatory signaling molecule), TNF-α (Tumor Necrosis Factor-alpha, a cytokine regulating inflammation), and IL-17 (Interleukin-17, a cytokine involved in immune response modulation), in patients with EOLP.
evidence: This is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 5H and gene expression analysis from scRNA-seq.

claim: Oral lichen planus (OLP) is a chronic inflammatory disease on the oral mucosa of unknown etiology mediated by T cells with a 1.01% global prevalence rate.
source: Oral lichen planus (OLP) is a chronic inflammatory disease on the oral mucosa of unknown etiology mediated by T cells with a 1.01% global prevalence rate (González-Moles et al., 2021; Jiang et al., 2022b).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to González-Moles et al., 2021 and Jiang et al., 2022b.

claim: EOLP has a significantly higher risk of malignant transformation than NEOLP.
source: Notably, EOLP has a significantly higher risk of malignant transformation than non-erosive oral lichen planus (NEOLP) (Arduino et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Arduino et al., 2021.

claim: The pathological feature of OLP is characterized by dense infiltration of T cells in the lamina propria, disruption of the basement membrane, and degeneration of basal keratinocytes.
source: The pathological feature of OLP is characterized by dense infiltration of T cells in the lamina propria, disruption of the basement membrane, and degeneration of basal keratinocytes (Xu et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Xu et al., 2022.

claim: CD8+ T cells are related to the liquefaction of basal cells in OLP.
source: CD8+ T cells are related to the liquefaction of basal cells
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the field.

claim: Tissue-resident memory T (Trm) cells are a recently described population of terminally differentiated T cells, which are crucial for local immunity.
source: Tissue-resident memory T (Trm) cells are a recently described population of terminally differentiated T cells, which are crucial for local immunity (Mueller et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Mueller et al., 2014.

claim: CD8+ Trm cells play important roles in the occurrence and development of many chronic inflammatory diseases such as psoriasis and vitiligo.
source: Recent studies had revealed that CD8+ Trm cells play important roles in the occurrence and development of many chronic inflammatory diseases such as psoriasis and vitiligo (Eberle et al., 2016; Richmond et al., 2018; Watanabe, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Eberle et al., 2016; Richmond et al., 2018; Watanabe, 2019.

claim: The final scRNA-seq dataset comprised 46,377 cells, with an average of 1743 genes per cell.
source: The final dataset comprised 46,377 cells, with an average of 1743 genes per cell.
evidence: This is a direct report of the experimental data obtained from scRNA-seq.

claim: Visualization using UMAP revealed 47 distinct cell clusters that were annotated as 8 major cell types.
source: Visualization using uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP) revealed 47 distinct cell clusters (Figure 1A) that were annotated as 8 major cell types (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by the UMAP analysis shown in Figure 1A and 1B.

claim: T cells constituted the highest proportion of all samples in the scRNA-seq analysis.
source: Surprisingly, although T cells, the hallmark cells of OLP, constituted the highest proportion of all samples
evidence: This is based on the cell composition analysis from scRNA-seq data.

claim: The proportion of B cells and myeloid cells increased in EOLP compared to NEOLP.
source: The cell composition analysis also revealed an increase in the proportion of B cells and myeloid cells in EOLP (Figure 1C, D).
evidence: This is supported by cell composition analysis shown in Figure 1C and 1D.

claim: Neutrophils were significantly more abundant in EOLP than NEOLP.
source: We observed that neutrophils were significantly more abundant in EOLP than NEOLP (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, B ).
evidence: This is supported by analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, B.

claim: Plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDC) were more common in EOLP compared to NEOLP.
source: Similarly, plasmacytoid (pDC) were also more common in EOLP compared to NEOLP.
evidence: This is based on myeloid cell analysis from scRNA-seq data.

claim: NEOLP had a higher number of myeloid dendritic cells (mDC) than EOLP.
source: However, NEOLP had a higher number of myeloid (mDC) than EOLP (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–D).
evidence: This is supported by analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–D.

claim: Neutrophil cells in EOLP were significantly enriched in defense response and positive regulation of cytokine production.
source: Upon conducting GO analysis, we found that neutrophil cells in EOLP were significantly enriched in defense response and positive regulation of cytokine production (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is supported by GO analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The NK/T cell population was divided into 23 cell subgroups by further clustering.
source: Subsequently, by further clustering, the genes of the NK/T cell population, the NK/T cell population was divided into a total of 23 cell subgroups (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: This is based on clustering analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, B.

claim: Six large cell subpopulations were identified in the NK/T cell population: NK cells, CD8+ T cells, CD4+ T cells, CD4+ CD8+ T cells, CD8+ Trm cells, and CD4+ CD8+ Trm cells.
source: After further annotation of the NK/T cell subsets with marker genes, six large cell subpopulations were described: NK cells, CD8+ T cells, CD4+ T cells, CD4+ CD8+ T cells, CD8+ Trm cells, and CD4+ CD8+ Trm cells (Figure 2A, B).
evidence: This is supported by annotation analysis shown in Figure 2A and 2B.

claim: EOLP exhibited fewer CD8+ T cells but more CD4+ T cells, CD8+ Trm cells, and CD4+ CD8+ T cells than NEOLP.
source: EOLP exhibited fewer CD8+ T cells but more CD4+ T cells, CD8+ Trm cells, and CD4+ CD8+ T cells than NEOLP.
evidence: This is based on cell proportion analysis from scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: LTB, an inflammatory response gene, was significantly active in the CD4+ T cells subset.
source: this study demonstrated that in the CD4+ T cells subset, LTB, an inflammatory response gene, was significantly active
evidence: This is based on gene expression analysis from scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: CCL4, CCL4L2, and CCL5 that guide immune cells to migrate to inflammatory sites were activated in CD8+ Trm and CD8+ T cells subsets.
source: while CCL4, CCL4L2, and CLL5 that guide immune cells to migrate to inflammatory sites were activated in CD8+ Trm and CD8+ T cells subset
evidence: This is based on gene expression analysis from scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The CD8+ T cell subset displayed significantly higher expression of GZMK compared to other subsets.
source: We observed that the CD8+ T cell subset displayed significantly higher expression of GZMK, a gene known to contribute to the cytotoxicity and induction of apoptosis in target cells, compared to other subsets.
evidence: This is based on gene expression analysis from scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: CD8+ Trm cells exhibited higher expression levels of GZMA, GZMK, TNF, PRF1, and other genes associated with inflammatory factors compared to other subgroups.
source: Moreover, CD8+ Trm cells in particular exhibited higher expression levels of GZMA, GZMK, TNF, PRF1, and other genes associated with inflammatory factors, when compared to other subgroups.
evidence: This is based on gene expression analysis from scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: B2M and HIF1A were found to be significantly expressed in EOLP compared to NEOLP.
source: Further analysis of the significantly different genes between NEOLP and EOLP indicated that B2M, closely related to the stability of MHC class I molecules and antigen presentation, and HIF1A, which regulates immune cell function and inflammation, were found to be significantly expressed in EOLP.
evidence: This is based on differential gene expression analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: EOLP expressed markers involved in the differentiation and function of Trm cells, including CD69, IL7R, CD7, and FOS.
source: Moreover, the EOLP expressed a number of markers involved in the differentiation and function of Trm cells, including CD69, IL7R, CD7, FOS, etc. (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A, Supplementary file 1a).
evidence: This is based on differential gene expression analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: CD69, GNLY, GZMB, IFNG, TNF, and PRF1 were significantly increased in the CD8+ Trm subgroup in EOLP compared to NEOLP.
source: we performed differential expression analysis and found that the CD8+Trm marker gene CD69, GNLY which can play a cytotoxic role, and multiple pro-inflammatory factor-related genes, such as GZMB, IFNG, TNF, and PRF1, were significantly increased in the CD8+ Trm subgroup in EOLP.
evidence: This is based on differential expression analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claim: CD8+ Trm differentially expressed genes in EOLP were more significantly enriched in pathways such as positive regulation of cytokine production, regulation of T cell activation, and positive regulation of cell activation.
source: GO enrichment analysis indicated that CD8+ Trm differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in EOLP between NEOLP were more significantly enriched in pathways such as positive regulation of cytokine production, regulation of T cell activation, and positive regulation of cell activation (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is based on GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 2F.

claim: CD8+ Trm cells may represent one of the terminal states of T cell differentiation and development in OLP.
source: The pseudotime analysis also suggests that CD8+ Trm cells may represent one of the terminal states of T cell differentiation and development in OLP (Figure 2G)
evidence: This is based on pseudotime analysis shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Spatial transcriptomics analysis was performed on normal oral mucosa (n = 2), NEOLP (n = 3), and EOLP (n = 1).
source: To investigate the spatial heterogeneity between normal oral mucosa and OLP, we performed the spatial transcriptomics (ST) analysis of normal oral mucosa (n = 2), NEOLP (n = 3), and EOLP (n = 1).
evidence: This is a direct report of the experimental design.

claim: Normal oral mucosa and NEOLP had intact epithelium in spatial transcriptomics analysis.
source: The normal oral mucosa and NEOLP had intact epithelium
evidence: This is based on spatial transcriptomics analysis shown in Figure 3A.

claim: In EOLP, the epithelium on one side of the tissue was intact while the epithelium on the other side was missing.
source: In EOLP, it can be seen that the epithelium on the left side of the tissue is intact, while the epithelium on the right side is missing (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is based on spatial transcriptomics analysis shown in Figure 3A.

claim: CD8+ Trm cells were more distributed in EOLP than NEOLP, and more distributed in NEOLP than normal oral mucosa.
source: it was found that CD8+ Trm cells were more distributed in EOLP than NEOLP, and more distributed in NEOLP than normal oral mucosa.
evidence: This is based on spatial transcriptomics analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: CD8+ Trm cells are mostly distributed adjacent to the epithelium in normal oral mucosa, NEOLP, and EOLP.
source: And it can be observed that whether in normal oral mucosa, NEOLP or EOLP, CD8+ Trm cells are mostly distributed adjacent to the epithelium
evidence: This is based on spatial transcriptomics analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: In EOLP tissues, CD8+ Trm cells in the areas where the epithelium is lost are correspondingly reduced.
source: while in EOLP tissues, CD8+ Trm cells in the areas where the epithelium is lost are correspondingly reduced, and there are CD8+ Trm cells in the deeper lamina propria of the corresponding tissues (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is based on spatial transcriptomics analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The expression of TNF, IL17A/IL17RA, and IFNGR1 was higher in OLP than in normal oral mucosa.
source: We observed that the expression of TNF, IL17A/IL17RA, IFNGR1, etc. was higher than in normal oral mucosa.
evidence: This is based on spatial transcriptomics analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The signals of IFNGR1 and IL17RA were significantly enhanced in EOLP compared with NEOLP.
source: And the signals of the effector receptor IFNGR1 of IFN and the effector receptor IL17RA of IL17 were significantly enhanced in EOLP compared with NEOLP.
evidence: This is based on spatial transcriptomics analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: A clinical cohort with 40 participants was established, confirmed by clinical manifestation and pathological diagnosis.
source: To objectively illustrate the molecular mechanism of OLP erosion, we established a clinical cohort with 40 participants, which were confirmed by clinical manifestation and pathological diagnosis.
evidence: This is a direct report of the study design.

claim: The NEOLP group included 15 females and 12 males, while the EOLP group included 8 females and 5 males.
source: there were 15 females and 12 males in the NEOLP group and 8 females and 5 males in the EOLP group.
evidence: This is demographic data from the clinical cohort shown in Table 1.

claim: The mean age of the NEOLP group was 30.07 ± 11.34 years and that of the EOLP group was 45.08 ± 12.86 years.
source: The mean age of the NEOLP group was 30.07 ± 11.34 years and that of the EOLP group was 45.08 ± 12.86 years.
evidence: This is demographic data from the clinical cohort shown in Table 1.

claim: The expression of ITGA1, LITAF, SKIL, TNFRSF6B, IL17RA, and IFNAR1 were significantly increased in EOLP compared to NEOLP.
source: Through differential gene analysis, it was found that in NEOLP and EOLP, the expression of multiple core factors and effector cytokines or their receptor transcription factors of CD8+ Trm cells, including ITGA1, LITAF, SKIL, etc., and related immune factor receptors such as TNFRSF6B, IL17RA, and IFNAR1 were significantly increased in the EOLP than in the NEOLP (Figure 4A, B; Table 2).
evidence: This is based on differential gene analysis from bulk RNA-seq shown in Figure 4A, B and Table 2.

claim: Multiple core factors and effector cytokines of CD8+ Trm cells were consistently upregulated in the recurrent erosion group compared to the persistent non-erosion group.
source: Moreover, the multiple core factors and effector cytokines of CD8+ Trm cells were found to be consistently upregulated in the recurrent erosion group, further supporting the role of CD8+ Trm cells in OLP progression (Figure 4C, D).
evidence: This is based on differential gene analysis from bulk RNA-seq shown in Figure 4C, D.

claim: The core genes of CD8+ Trm cells are closely related to the clinical manifestations of OLP.
source: We found that the core genes of CD8+ Trm cells are closely related to the clinical manifestations of OLP
evidence: This is based on multivariate logistic regression analysis shown in Table 2.

claim: The expression differences of ITGA1, LITAF, SKIL, IL17RA, IFNG41, IFNAR1, and TNFRSF6B were statistically significant between NEOLP and EOLP.
source: the expression differences of marker genes such as ITGA1, LITAF, SKIL, and cytokine-related genes such as IL17RA, IFNG41, IFNAR1, and TNFRSF6B were statistically significant between the two clinical types.
evidence: This is based on multivariate logistic regression analysis shown in Table 2.

claim: CD69, ITGA1, LITAF, SKIL, IL17RA, IFNG41, IFNAR1, and GZMB expression differences were statistically significant between persistent non-erosion and recurrent erosion groups.
source: Marker genes such as CD69, ITGA1, LITAF, SKIL, and cytokine-related genes such as IL17RA, IFNG41, IFNAR1, and GZMB are associated with two clinical outcomes of persistent non-erosion and recurrent erosion. The differences in expression were statistically significant and were significantly increased in the recurrent erosion group (Table 2).
evidence: This is based on multivariate logistic regression analysis shown in Table 2.

claim: The content of CD8+ Trm cells in EOLP was significantly increased compared to NEOLP as verified by immunofluorescence.
source: Immunofluorescence experiments verified that there were CD8+ Trm cells in NEOLP and EOLP. The content of CD8+ Trm cells in EOLP was significantly increased than that in NEOLP.
evidence: This is based on immunofluorescence experiments shown in Figure 5A-D.

claim: CD8+ Trm cells are mostly close to the basal layer in OLP tissues.
source: It can be seen from the location that CD8+ Trm cells are mostly close to the basal layer.
evidence: This is based on immunofluorescence experiments shown in Figure 5A-D.

claim: In EOLP, CD8+ Trm cells accumulated more obviously under the erosive epithelium compared to NEOLP.
source: while in EOLP, CD8+ Trm cells accumulated more obviously under the erosive epithelium, and the number was obviously higher than in NEOLP
evidence: This is based on immunofluorescence experiments shown in Figure 5C-D.

claim: The content of CD8+ Trm cells in EOLP was significantly higher than that in NEOLP as measured by flow cytometry.
source: it was found that the content of CD8+ Trm cells in EOLP was significantly higher than that in NEOLP (p < 0.05) (Figure 5F, G).
evidence: This is based on flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 5F, G.

claim: CD8+ Trm cells in EOLP produced significantly higher levels of TNF-α, IFN-γ, and IL17 than those in NEOLP.
source: Our results showed that CD8+ Trm cells in EOLP produced significantly higher levels of the inflammatory cytokines TNF-α, IFN-γ, and IL17 than those in NEOLP, with the increase in IFN-γ being statistically significant (Figure 5H).
evidence: This is based on ELISA analysis shown in Figure 5H.

claim: This study is the first to provide a comprehensive characterization of the presence, spatial distribution, and heterogeneity of CD8+ Trm cells in OLP tissues with different clinical manifestations.
source: This study is the first to provide a comprehensive characterization of the presence, spatial distribution, and heterogeneity of CD8+ Trm cells in OLP tissues with different clinical manifestations
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the study.

claim: CD8+ Trm cells play a crucial role in the pathological process of OLP.
source: Our findings suggest that CD8+ Trm cells play a crucial role in the pathological process of OLP
evidence: This is an inference based on the collective data presented in the study.

claim: CD8+ Trm cells contribute to the erosion of OLP by secreting multiple cytokines.
source: CD8+ Trm cells play a crucial role in the pathological process of OLP and contribute to the erosion of OLP by secreting multiple cytokines.
evidence: This is an inference based on the collective data presented in the study, including scRNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics, and ELISA results.

claim: CD8+ Trm cells represent one of the terminal states of T cells in OLP.
source: Pseudo-time analysis revealed that CD8+ Trm cells represent one of the terminal states of T cells in OLP.
evidence: This is based on pseudotime analysis shown in Figure 2G.

claim: CD8+ Trm cells may affect the biological process of OLP by releasing cytokines such as TNF, IFN, and IL17.
source: CD8+ Trm cells may affect the biological process of OLP by releasing cytokines such as TNF, IFN, IL17
evidence: This is an inference based on gene expression and protein secretion data.

claim: The activity of CD8+ Trm cells was enhanced in EOLP compared to NEOLP.
source: the activity of CD8+ Trm cells was enhanced in EOLP.
evidence: This is based on differential gene expression and GO enrichment analysis.

claim: CD8+ Trm cells can produce IFN-γ, which is a key cytokine in response to viral infection.
source: Previous studies have found that CD8+ Trm cells can produce IFN-γ, which is a key cytokine in response to viral infection (Cheuk et al., 2017; Guidotti et al., 1996).

claim: CD8+ Trm cells can produce perforin and granzyme B upon IL15 stimulation to mediate cytotoxic responses.
source: CD8+ Trms can also produce perforin and granzyme B upon IL15 stimulation to mediate cytotoxic responses that respond to infections by enhancing local immune responses (Cheuk et al., 2017).

source: In addition, IFN-γ upregulates the production of vascular cell adhesion molecule-1, which recruits central memory T cells (TCM) and B cells to the site of Trm cell localization (Ariotti et al., 2014).

claim: CD8+ Trm cells play a crucial part in the recurring aggravation of psoriasis.
source: Similarly, CD8+ Trm cells also play a crucial part in the recurring aggravation of psoriasis.

claim: CD8+ Trm cells can still be detected in the skin that seems normal after psoriatic skin lesions have disappeared.
source: Even after the psoriatic skin lesions have disappeared, CD8+ Trm cells can still be detected in the skin that seems normal.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about psoriasis.

claim: CD8+ Trm cells in psoriasis have the potential to escalate local inflammation over time and trigger recurrent attacks at the same site.
source: These cells have the potential to escalate local inflammation over time, trigger recurrent attacks at the same site, and generate a domino effect of inflammation (Owczarczyk Saczonek et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Owczarczyk Saczonek et al., 2020.

claim: CD8+ Trm cells in EOLP tissue have enhanced ability to produce inflammatory cytokines such as IFN-γ compared with NEOLP.
source: An ELISA test confirmed that CD8+ Trm cells in EOLP tissue have enhanced ability to produce inflammatory cytokines such as IFN-γ compared with NEOLP

claim: CD8+ Trm cells protect the host against viruses by producing IFN-γ in lung tissue.
source: Previous evidence suggests that CD8+ Trm cells protect the host against viruses by producing IFN-γ in lung tissue (Jiang et al., 2022a).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Jiang et al., 2022a.

claim: Recurrent episodes of autoimmune diseases are believed to be due, in part, to the persistence of local Trm cells that are difficult to eliminate entirely.
source: Recurrent episodes of autoimmune diseases are believed to be due, in part, to the persistence of local Trm cells that are difficult to eliminate entirely (Jiang et al., 2012; Owczarczyk Saczonek et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Jiang et al., 2012 and Owczarczyk Saczonek et al., 2020.

claim: CD8+ Trm cells are primarily distributed in the lamina propria close to the basement membrane in OLP.
source: These cells are primarily distributed in the lamina propria close to the basement membrane

source: The release of excess cytokines such as IFN-γ may influence the clinical types and outcomes of OLP

source: CD8+ Trm cells may be a great important promoting factor for the recurrent erosion of OLP

claim: CD8+ Trm cells may become a potential immunotherapy target for OLP treatment.
